title: Your first 30 days operating a vending machine
excerpt: Use an opening-month plan to test payments, refine your first stock mix and set a restocking rhythm.
opening: The first month is a test of demand and of the work needed to serve the site. A sold-out row can make a weak-looking sales report difficult to interpret. Track availability alongside sales and keep the first changes small enough to understand.
checklist: Before opening, test a purchase and refund path, confirm product prices, and save the machine ID and service contacts. Check dispensing with each initial pack type.
In week one, start with a small range. Record the units loaded by slot, date and expiry. Rotate stock so the shortest valid dates are used first.
At each visit, log units left, stockouts, near-expiry items, time on site and any faults. Reconcile the machine count and payment records.
In week two, set refill quantities using sales between visits, a small buffer for faster items and the shelf life of each product. Review the buffer if waste grows.
In week three, change one clear variable at a time, such as one slow product or one price. Note the change date, site events and any interruptions.
In week four, compare units per trading day, refill travel, waste and faults. Choose one product change and one operational improvement for the next month.
close: Preserve the opening records as your comparison point. Track recurring failures by time, product and slot so the service team can investigate with specific examples.
